one_line: Pratihāra-era Sanskrit poet-critic of Kannauj, author of the Kāvya­mīmāṃsā and theorist of poetry, reuse, and a mapped literary world.

appearance.age_look: mid-40s, lean scholar’s build with upright posture
appearance.face: oval face with sharp nose and high cheekbones, medium-brown North Indian complexion, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, small tilaka on the forehead, calm observant eyes with a faint, knowing half-smile as default expression
appearance.hair: rich black hair gathered into a short, tidy topknot at the back of the crown, sides smoothly combed; simple narrow ochre headband tied around the topknot, no other headwear
appearance.costume: era-accurate Pratihāra-period scholar’s attire: a long-sleeved, waist-length cotton uttariya in soft cream white draped over both shoulders and crossing the chest, worn above a finely woven ankle-length dhoti in muted sandalwood beige with a narrow maroon border, pleated neatly in front; over this, a light saffron-yellow shawl (angavastra) with thin brown edge bands wrapped around the torso and hanging evenly from both shoulders; simple leather sandals on the feet, a thin dark brown waist cord barely visible at the dhoti’s fold, and modest gold stud earrings with a single small bead, plus a plain wooden-bead mala around the neck to signal his scholarly-ascetic discipline.
appearance.signature: a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a dark red cord in his left hand, and a slender stylus held lightly in his right, as if ready to annotate the Kāvya­mīmāṃsā’s discussion of poetic training, borrowing, and the mapping of regions and cities.

ref_desc: Rājaśekhara is a mid-40s lean scholar with an oval medium-brown face, black topknot and ochre headband, cream uttariya, beige dhoti with maroon border, saffron shawl, simple ornaments, and a palm-leaf manuscript with stylus in cream, saffron, beige, maroon, and dark brown tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Rājaśekhara, a dignified Pratihāra-era Sanskrit scholar in his mid-40s with a lean build, oval medium-brown face, sharp nose, high cheekbones, small tilaka and calm, intelligent eyes framed by a short neatly trimmed beard and moustache. His rich black hair is gathered into a tidy topknot at the back of the crown, encircled by a simple narrow ochre headband. Dress him in a cream white long-sleeved waist-length uttariya draped over both shoulders and crossing his chest, over an ankle-length sandalwood beige dhoti with a narrow maroon border, pleated cleanly in front. Wrap a light saffron-yellow angavastra shawl with thin brown edge bands around his torso, hanging evenly from both shoulders, and put simple leather sandals on his feet. Add modest gold stud earrings with a small bead and a plain wooden-bead mala at his neck to signal devotion to learning. In his left hand he holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a dark red cord, and in his right he lightly grips a slender stylus, as if ready to annotate ideas about poetic inspiration, training, literary borrowing, and mapping regions and cities. Use a palette dominated by cream white, saffron yellow, sandalwood beige, maroon, and dark brown, and present him front-facing with clear head-to-toe details for consistent redrawing.
